records.source: וָאֶרְאֶ֗ה וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֶל־הָרָקִ֨יעַ֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הַכְּרֻבִ֔ים כְּאֶ֣בֶן סַפִּ֔יר כְּמַרְאֵ֖ה דְּמ֣וּת כִּסֵּ֑א נִרְאָ֖ה עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I looked, and behold, on the vault that [was] over [the] head of the cherubim, like a stone of sapphire, like [the] appearance of [the] likeness of a throne, appeared above them.
pieces: I looked, and on the vault above the heads of the cherubim I saw something that looked like a sapphire stone, something that looked like a throne, appearing above them.

L.1: And I looked, and look, on the vault that [was] above the head of the cherubim [there was something] like a sapphire stone, like the appearance of the likeness of a throne, appearing above them.

R.1: Then I looked up. Above the heads of the cherubim was a dome. On it, high above the cherubim, was something that looked like a throne made of sapphire, a deep blue stone.

decisions.choice: cherubim: winged heavenly creatures who guard the holy presence of God and bear his throne
decisions.reason: In the Bible cherubim guard the way to the tree of life (Genesis 3:24), spread their wings over the ark (Exodus 25:18-22), are carved and woven throughout the tabernacle and temple (Exodus 26:1; 1 Kings 6:23-35), and carry the LORD, who rides on a cherub (Psalm 18:11) and is "enthroned on the cherubim" (1 Samuel 4:4). Across the ancient Near East, great winged creatures with features of humans and animals guarded palaces, thrones and temples. Cherubim are not the winged children of later art. In this chapter Ezekiel recognizes the living creatures of chapter 1 as cherubim (10:15, 20).

decisions.choice: like a sapphire stone, like the appearance of the likeness of a throne: the guarded way of describing the vision (see 1:28)
decisions.reason: As in 1:26, Ezekiel sees a throne but describes it only by likenesses; see 1:28. The throne is empty in this verse, and its rider is not described again.

decisions.choice: sapphire: a deep blue precious stone, probably lapis lazuli
alternatives: the blue gem now called sapphire
decisions.reason: The same stone is under the feet of the God of Israel in Exodus 24:10 and forms the throne in 1:26. The stone called sapphire today was little known in Israel at the time, and the word probably meant lapis lazuli, a deep blue stone flecked with gold.

decisions.choice: cherubim (all levels); vault (L, B); dome (R)
decisions.reason: "Cherubim" is kept at every level, with the culture decision (m1) for readers who do not know the word. "Vault" and "dome" are the settled words for the structure above the creatures in chapter 1, as in Genesis 1:6.

records.heading: The cherubim and the glory

records.source: וַיֹּ֜אמֶר אֶל־הָאִ֣ישׁ׀לְבֻ֣שׁ הַבַּדִּ֗ים וַיֹּ֡אמֶר בֹּא֩ אֶל־בֵּינ֨וֹת לַגַּלְגַּ֜ל אֶל־תַּ֣חַת לַכְּר֗וּב וּמַלֵּ֨א חָפְנֶ֤יךָ גַֽחֲלֵי־אֵשׁ֙ מִבֵּינ֣וֹת לַכְּרֻבִ֔ים וּזְרֹ֖ק עַל־הָעִ֑יר וַיָּבֹ֖א לְעֵינָֽי׃
records.gloss: And he spoke to the man clothed [in] the linen and said, Go in between the whirling wheels, to beneath the cherub, and fill your hands [with] coals of fire from between the cherubim, and scatter over the city. And he went in before my eyes.
pieces: He said to the man dressed in linen, "Go in among the whirling wheels beneath the cherub. Take two handfuls of burning coals from among the cherubim and toss them over the city." He went in while I watched.

L.2: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to the man clothed in linen and said, "Enter in between the whirling wheels, below the cherub, and fill the hollows of your hands [with] coals of fire from between the cherubim, and toss [them] over the city." And he went in before my eyes.

R.2: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to the man dressed in linen, "Go in among the whirling wheels under the cherubim. Fill both hands with hot coals from among the cherubim and throw them on the city." I watched him go in.

decisions.choice: whirling wheels: the wheels of chapter 1, named for their whirling
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning "to roll" and is used of a wheel (Isaiah 5:28) and of a whirlwind (Psalm 77:19). Ezekiel hears the wheels given this name in 10:13.

decisions.choice: coals of fire scattered over the city: judgment by fire from God's own presence
decisions.reason: In 1:13 fire moved back and forth among the living creatures. In Isaiah 6:6-7 a coal from the altar cleanses the prophet; here the coals from beside the throne are thrown over the city in judgment. Jerusalem was burned by the Babylonians in 586 BC (2 Kings 25:9).

decisions.choice: the cherub: the singular stands for the cherubim as a whole
decisions.reason: Ezekiel moves between "the cherub" and "the cherubim" in this chapter (9:3; 10:2, 4, 7). The singular here refers to the group, as the plural in the same verse shows.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said; under the cherubim
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker and uses the plural, so that the reader is not left to work out who is speaking and that "the cherub" means the group (m3).

records.source: וְהַכְּרֻבִ֗ים עֹֽמְדִ֛ים מִימִ֥ין לַבַּ֖יִת בְּבֹא֣וֹ הָאִ֑ישׁ וְהֶעָנָ֣ן מָלֵ֔א אֶת־הֶחָצֵ֖ר הַפְּנִימִֽית׃
records.gloss: And the cherubim [were] standing on [the] right [side] of the house in the going in of the man; and the cloud filled the court the inner.
pieces: The cherubim were standing on the south side of the temple when the man went in, and a cloud filled the inner court.

L.3: Now the cherubim were standing at the right of the house when the man entered, and the cloud filled the inner court.

R.3: The cherubim were standing on the south side of the temple when the man went in. A cloud filled the inner courtyard.

decisions.choice: the right side of the house: the south side
decisions.reason: The temple faced east, so its right side was the south. The cherubim stand away from the north side, where the idols of chapter 8 were.

decisions.choice: the cloud filled the court: the sign of the LORD's presence, as when the tabernacle and the temple were first filled
decisions.reason: A cloud filled the tabernacle and Solomon's temple when the glory of the LORD came to dwell there (Exodus 40:34-35; 1 Kings 8:10-11). Here the same signs mark the glory's going away.

decisions.choice: the south side
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "right"; Balanced and Readable give the direction meant (m1).

records.source: וַיָּ֤רָם כְּבוֹד־יְהוָה֙ מֵעַ֣ל הַכְּר֔וּב עַ֖ל מִפְתַּ֣ן הַבָּ֑יִת וַיִּמָּלֵ֤א הַבַּ֨יִת֙ אֶת־הֶ֣עָנָ֔ן וְהֶֽחָצֵר֙ מָֽלְאָ֔ה אֶת־נֹ֖גַהּ כְּב֥וֹד יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And rose [the] glory of Yahweh from above the cherub to [the] threshold of the house; and was filled the house [with] the cloud, and the court was filled [with] the brightness of [the] glory of Yahweh.
pieces: Then the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rose from above the cherub and moved to the threshold of the temple. Cloud filled the temple, and the court was flooded with the radiance of the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.4: And the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rose from above the cherub [to go] to the threshold of the house; and the house was filled by the cloud, and the court was full of the glow of the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.4: The glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rose up from above the cherubim and moved to the doorway of the temple. The cloud filled the temple, and the courtyard was full of the bright light of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s glory.

decisions.choice: the glory rose to the threshold: the move already told in 9:3
decisions.reason: The verse goes back to the step reported in 9:3, as the vision returns from the man in linen to the glory. The next stage of the glory's departure follows in 10:18-19 (see 9:3).

decisions.choice: bright light
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer phrase for the brightness that shines from the glory.

records.source: וְקוֹל֙ כַּנְפֵ֣י הַכְּרוּבִ֔ים נִשְׁמַ֕ע עַד־הֶחָצֵ֖ר הַחִיצֹנָ֑ה כְּק֥וֹל אֵל־שַׁדַּ֖י בְּדַבְּרֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And [the] sound of [the] wings of the cherubim was heard as far as the court the outer, like [the] voice of God Almighty in his speaking.
pieces: The sound of the cherubim's wings carried to the outer court. It was like the voice of God Almighty when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} speaks.

L.5: And the sound of the wings of the cherubim was heard up to the outer court, like the voice of God Almighty in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} speaking.

R.5: The noise of the cherubim's wings could be heard all the way to the outer courtyard. It sounded like the voice of God All-Powerful when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} speaks.

decisions.choice: like the voice of God Almighty: the thunder of 1:24
decisions.reason: In 1:24 the wings of the living creatures sounded "like the voice of the Almighty". Thunder is called the voice of the LORD in Psalm 29:3-9. "God Almighty" is the name by which God made himself known to Abraham (Genesis 17:1; Exodus 6:3).

decisions.choice: God All-Powerful
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this name: "the Almighty" at Literal and Balanced, "God All-Powerful" at Readable.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י בְּצַוֺּתוֹ֙ אֶת־הָאִ֤ישׁ לְבֻֽשׁ־הַבַּדִּים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר קַ֥ח אֵשׁ֙ מִבֵּינ֣וֹת לַגַּלְגַּ֔ל מִבֵּינ֖וֹת לַכְּרוּבִ֑ים וַיָּבֹא֙ וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֔ד אֵ֖צֶל הָאוֹפָֽן׃
records.gloss: And it was, in his commanding the man clothed [in] the linen, saying, Take fire from between the whirling wheels, from between the cherubim, and he went in and stood beside the wheel.
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had given the man dressed in linen the command, "Take fire from among the whirling wheels, from among the cherubim," the man went in and stood beside one of the wheels.

L.6: And it came about, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had commanded the man clothed in linen, "Take fire from among the whirling wheels, from among the cherubim," that he went in and stood beside the wheel.

R.6: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} commanded the man dressed in linen, "Take fire from among the whirling wheels, from among the cherubim." So the man went in and stood beside a wheel.

decisions.choice: the command of 10:2 taken up again
decisions.reason: After the description of the cherubim and the glory in 10:3-5, the narrative returns to the order given to the man in linen in 10:2 and tells how it was carried out.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} commanded
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD as the one who gives the command, as in 10:2, and splits the sentence.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ הַכְּר֨וּב אֶת־יָד֜וֹ מִבֵּינ֣וֹת לַכְּרוּבִ֗ים אֶל־הָאֵשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ בֵּינ֣וֹת הַכְּרֻבִ֔ים וַיִּשָּׂא֙ וַיִּתֵּ֔ן אֶל־חָפְנֵ֖י לְבֻ֣שׁ הַבַּדִּ֑ים וַיִּקַּ֖ח וַיֵּצֵֽא׃
records.gloss: And stretched out the cherub his hand from between the cherubim to the fire that [was] between the cherubim, and lifted and put into [the] hands of [the one] clothed [in] the linen; and he took and went out.
pieces: Then one of the cherubim reached out its hand from among the cherubim to the fire that was among them. It took some and put it into the hands of the man dressed in linen, who took it and went out.

L.7: And the cherub put out its hand from between the cherubim toward the fire that [was] between the cherubim, and lifted [some] and put [it] into the hands of the one clothed in linen; and he took [it] and went out.

R.7: One of the cherubim reached out its hand toward the fire among them. It picked up some of the fire and put it into the hands of the man dressed in linen. He took it and went out.

decisions.choice: he took it and went out: the fire goes out to the city
decisions.reason: The vision does not describe the burning. The man in linen, who marked the faithful (9:4), also carries out the fire that will fall on the city (10:2).

decisions.choice: its hand
decisions.reason: Hebrew has no neuter, and the cherub is grammatically masculine. Each level calls a cherub "it", since the cherubim are creatures, not men.

records.source: וַיֵּרָ֖א לַכְּרֻבִ֑ים תַּבְנִית֙ יַד־אָדָ֔ם תַּ֖חַת כַּנְפֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And appeared for the cherubim [the] form of a hand of a human beneath their wings.
pieces: Under their wings the cherubim could be seen to have something that looked like human hands.

L.8: And there appeared on the cherubim the form of a human hand beneath their wings.

R.8: Under the wings of the cherubim I could see something that looked like human hands.

decisions.choice: the form of a human hand under their wings: as the living creatures of 1:8
decisions.reason: The hand that reached into the fire in 10:7 was like the hands Ezekiel saw under the wings of the living creatures (1:8). "The form of" is one of the cautious expressions of the vision (see 1:28).

records.source: וָאֶרְאֶ֗ה וְהִנֵּ֨ה אַרְבָּעָ֣ה אוֹפַנִּים֮ אֵ֣צֶל הַכְּרוּבִים֒ אוֹפַ֣ן אֶחָ֗ד אֵ֚צֶל הַכְּר֣וּב אֶחָ֔ד וְאוֹפַ֣ן אֶחָ֔ד אֵ֖צֶל הַכְּר֣וּב אֶחָ֑ד וּמַרְאֵה֙ הָא֣וֹפַנִּ֔ים כְּעֵ֖ין אֶ֥בֶן תַּרְשִֽׁישׁ׃
records.gloss: And I looked, and behold, four wheels beside the cherubim, wheel one beside the cherub one, and wheel one beside the cherub one; and [the] appearance of the wheels [was] like [the] gleam of a stone of Tarshish.
pieces: I looked, and there were four wheels beside the cherubim, one wheel beside each cherub. The wheels gleamed like chrysolite.

L.9: And I looked, and look, four wheels beside the cherubim, one wheel beside one cherub and one wheel beside one cherub; and the appearance of the wheels [was] like the gleam of chrysolite.

R.9: I looked and saw four wheels beside the cherubim, one beside each of them. The wheels sparkled like a gem called chrysolite.

decisions.choice: chrysolite: the precious stone called tarshish, as in 1:16
decisions.reason: The stone is named in 1:16, where the note explains it, and it was set in the high priest's breastpiece (Exodus 28:20). Its exact kind is not certain.

decisions.choice: four wheels beside the cherubim: the wheels of 1:15-21
decisions.reason: Ezekiel describes again what he saw by the Kebar, now beside the cherubim in the temple.

decisions.choice: a gem called chrysolite
decisions.reason: Readable reuses the wording of 1:16, which says that chrysolite is a gem.

records.source: וּמַ֨רְאֵיהֶ֔ם דְּמ֥וּת אֶחָ֖ד לְאַרְבַּעְתָּ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יִהְיֶ֥ה הָאוֹפַ֖ן בְּת֥וֹךְ הָאוֹפָֽן׃
records.gloss: And their appearance, one likeness to the four of them, as if would be the wheel in [the] midst of the wheel.
pieces: As for their appearance, all four had the same form, as if a wheel were inside a wheel.

L.10: And as for their appearance, the four of them had one likeness, as if a wheel were in the midst of a wheel.

R.10: All four wheels looked alike. Each one looked like a wheel inside another wheel.

decisions.choice: a wheel in the midst of a wheel: two wheels set crosswise, so that they could roll in any direction
alternatives: a smaller wheel inside a larger one
decisions.reason: The phrase repeats 1:16. It is usually understood as two wheels crossing at right angles, which explains why the wheels could go in any of four directions without turning (10:11). The text does not describe the design further.

records.source: בְּלֶכְתָּ֗ם אֶל־אַרְבַּ֤עַת רִבְעֵיהֶם֙ יֵלֵ֔כוּ לֹ֥א יִסַּ֖בּוּ בְּלֶכְתָּ֑ם כִּ֣י הַמָּק֞וֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִפְנֶ֤ה הָרֹאשׁ֙ אַחֲרָ֣יו יֵלֵ֔כוּ לֹ֥א יִסַּ֖בּוּ בְּלֶכְתָּֽם׃
records.gloss: In their going, to their four sides they went; not they turned in their going, for [to] the place that faced the head, after it they went; not they turned in their going.
pieces: When they moved, they could go in any of the four directions without turning as they went. Wherever the head faced, the wheels followed it, without turning as they went.

L.11: When they went, they went toward [any of] their four sides; they did not turn as they went; for to the place toward which the head faced, they went after it; they did not turn as they went.

R.11: When they moved, they could go in any of the four directions without turning. They went wherever the front faced, and they did not turn as they moved.

decisions.choice: the head: the front, the direction one of them faced
alternatives: the head of the leading cherub
the head of the whole throne-chariot
decisions.reason: The word means "head", and also "first" or "front". It probably means that the whole company moved in the direction the front was facing, as in 1:9, 12. It may refer to the head of one cherub that led the others.

decisions.choice: the front
decisions.reason: Readable says "the front", the sense most likely meant (m1).

records.source: וְכָל־בְּשָׂרָם֙ וְגַבֵּהֶ֔ם וִֽידֵיהֶ֖ם וְכַנְפֵיהֶ֑ם וְהָאֽוֹפַנִּ֗ים מְלֵאִ֤ים עֵינַ֨יִם֙ סָבִ֔יב לְאַרְבַּעְתָּ֖ם אוֹפַנֵּיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And all their flesh, and their backs, and their hands, and their wings, and the wheels, [were] full of eyes all around; the four of them [had] their wheels.
pieces: Their whole bodies, their backs, their hands and their wings, and the wheels too, were full of eyes all around, the wheels that the four of them had.

L.12: And all their flesh, their backs, their hands, their wings, and the wheels: full of eyes all around; the four of them [had] their wheels.

R.12: Their whole bodies were covered with eyes, their backs, their hands and their wings. The wheels that belonged to the four of them were covered with eyes too.

decisions.choice: their whole body: the bodies of the cherubim, or of the wheels
alternatives: the rims and parts of the wheels only
decisions.reason: The pronoun "their" may refer to the cherubim or to the wheels. In 1:18 it is the rims of the wheels that are full of eyes; here the list includes hands and wings, which suits the cherubim.

decisions.choice: full of eyes: nothing is hidden from the one enthroned above them
decisions.reason: The leaders said "the LORD does not see" (8:12; 9:9). The throne of the LORD is covered with eyes.

records.source: לָא֖וֹפַנִּ֑ים לָהֶ֛ם קוֹרָ֥א הַגַּלְגַּ֖ל בְּאָזְנָֽי׃
records.gloss: To the wheels, to them it was called, The whirling wheels, in my ears.
pieces: As for the wheels, I heard them called "the whirling wheels."

L.13: As for the wheels, they were named in my hearing "the whirling wheels."

R.13: I heard someone call the wheels "the whirling wheels."

decisions.choice: "the whirling wheels": a name given to the wheels (see 10:2)
alternatives: "Whirl!", a command to the wheels to move
decisions.reason: The word can be a name or a call. Ezekiel hears it spoken, and he has already used it for the wheels in 10:2 and 10:6, so it is taken as their name.

records.source: וְאַרְבָּעָ֥ה פָנִ֖ים לְאֶחָ֑ד פְּנֵ֨י הָאֶחָ֜ד פְּנֵ֣י הַכְּר֗וּב וּפְנֵ֤י הַשֵּׁנִי֙ פְּנֵ֣י אָדָ֔ם וְהַשְּׁלִישִׁי֙ פְּנֵ֣י אַרְיֵ֔ה וְהָרְבִיעִ֖י פְּנֵי־נָֽשֶׁר׃
records.gloss: And four faces to each one: [the] face of the one, [the] face of the cherub, and [the] face of the second, [the] face of a human, and the third, [the] face of a lion, and the fourth, [the] face of an eagle.
pieces: Each one had four faces: the first was the face of a cherub, the second a human face, the third a lion's face and the fourth an eagle's face.

L.14: And each one had four faces: the face of the first [was] the face of the cherub, and the face of the second the face of a human, and the third a lion's face, and the fourth an eagle's face.

R.14: Each cherub had four faces. The first was the face of a cherub. The second was a human face, the third a lion's face and the fourth an eagle's face.

decisions.choice: the face of the cherub: in place of the ox of 1:10
decisions.reason: In 1:10 the four faces are a human, a lion, an ox and an eagle. Here "the face of the cherub" takes the place of the ox, so the cherub's own face was probably that of a bull, like the winged bulls that guarded palace gates in Mesopotamia. The Septuagint does not have this verse.

decisions.choice: the face of a human: the word for humankind, not a man in particular
decisions.reason: The word is the one used in "son of man" (see 2:1). It means a human being in general.

records.source: וַיֵּרֹ֖מּוּ הַכְּרוּבִ֑ים הִ֣יא הַחַיָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִ֖יתִי בִּֽנְהַר־כְּבָֽר׃
records.gloss: And rose up the cherubim; that [was] the living creature that I had seen by [the] river Kebar.
pieces: Then the cherubim rose up. These were the living creatures I had seen by the Kebar Canal.

L.15: And the cherubim rose up. That [was] the living creature that I had seen by the river Kebar.

R.15: Then the cherubim rose into the air. They were the same living creatures I had seen by the Kebar Canal.

decisions.choice: the cherubim are the living creatures of chapter 1
decisions.reason: Ezekiel now identifies the four living creatures he saw in Babylon (1:5-14) with the cherubim of the temple. The throne of the LORD that he saw among the exiles is the same throne that is now leaving Jerusalem. He says it again in 10:20 and 10:22.

decisions.choice: the living creature: a singular for the four together
decisions.reason: Ezekiel uses the singular for the whole group here and in 10:17 and 10:20, as in 1:20-22, as if the four formed one living being.

decisions.choice: These were the living creatures; the Kebar Canal
alternatives: That was the living creature; the river Kebar
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural, which English needs to refer to the four cherubim (m2). "Living creatures" is the settled wording at every level. "The river Kebar" (Literal) and "the Kebar Canal" (Balanced, Readable) follow 1:1.

records.source: וּבְלֶ֨כֶת֙ הַכְּרוּבִ֔ים יֵלְכ֥וּ הָאוֹפַנִּ֖ים אֶצְלָ֑ם וּבִשְׂאֵ֨ת הַכְּרוּבִ֜ים אֶת־כַּנְפֵיהֶ֗ם לָרוּם֙ מֵעַ֣ל הָאָ֔רֶץ לֹא־יִסַּ֧בּוּ הָאוֹפַנִּ֛ים גַּם־הֵ֖ם מֵאֶצְלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And in the going of the cherubim, went the wheels beside them; and in the lifting of the cherubim their wings to rise from upon the earth, not turned the wheels, even they, from beside them.
pieces: When the cherubim moved, the wheels moved beside them, and when the cherubim spread their wings to rise from the ground, the wheels stayed at their side.

L.16: And as the cherubim moved, the wheels moved beside them; and as the cherubim raised their wings to rise from the earth, the wheels likewise did not turn from beside them.

R.16: When the cherubim moved, the wheels moved with them. When the cherubim spread their wings to rise from the ground, the wheels stayed right beside them.

decisions.choice: the wheels moved with the cherubim: as in 1:19-21
decisions.reason: The wheels have no motion of their own; they go, stop and rise with the creatures (10:17).

records.source: בְּעָמְדָ֣ם יַעֲמֹ֔דוּ וּבְרוֹמָ֖ם יֵר֣וֹמּוּ אוֹתָ֑ם כִּ֛י ר֥וּחַ הַחַיָּ֖ה בָּהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: In their standing they stood, and in their rising they rose with them; for [the] spirit of the living creature [was] in them.
pieces: When the cherubim stood still, the wheels stood still, and when they rose, the wheels rose with them, for the spirit of the living creatures was in them.

L.17: When they stood still, these stood still, and when they rose, these rose with them; because the spirit of the living creature [was] in them.

R.17: When the cherubim stopped, the wheels stopped. When the cherubim rose, the wheels rose with them, because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.

decisions.choice: the spirit of the living creature: the life and will that moved the creatures, at work in the wheels too
decisions.reason: The words repeat 1:20-21. "Spirit" here is the force that drove the creatures (1:12), so the wheels moved as one with them.

decisions.choice: the cherubim; the wheels
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say which "they" is which, since the Hebrew uses pronouns only.

records.source: וַיֵּצֵא֙ כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֔ה מֵעַ֖ל מִפְתַּ֣ן הַבָּ֑יִת וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד עַל־הַכְּרוּבִֽים׃
records.gloss: And went out [the] glory of Yahweh from over [the] threshold of the house and stood over the cherubim.
pieces: Then the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} went out from the threshold of the temple and stopped above the cherubim.

L.18: Then the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} departed from over the threshold of the house and stood above the cherubim.

R.18: Then the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} left the doorway of the temple and moved to a place above the cherubim.

decisions.choice: the glory of the LORD goes out of the temple
decisions.reason: This is the second stage of the glory's departure (see 9:3). The glory, which filled the temple at its dedication (1 Kings 8:10-11), leaves it and mounts the throne carried by the cherubim. When the ark was taken in Eli's day, the cry was "The glory has departed from Israel" (1 Samuel 4:21-22).

records.source: וַיִּשְׂא֣וּ הַכְּרוּבִ֣ים אֶת־כַּ֠נְפֵיהֶם וַיֵּר֨וֹמּוּ מִן־הָאָ֤רֶץ לְעֵינַי֙ בְּצֵאתָ֔ם וְהָאֽוֹפַנִּ֖ים לְעֻמָּתָ֑ם וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֗ד פֶּ֣תַח שַׁ֤עַר בֵּית־יְהוָה֙ הַקַּדְמוֹנִ֔י וּכְב֧וֹד אֱלֹהֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מִלְמָֽעְלָה׃
records.gloss: And lifted the cherubim their wings and rose from the earth before my eyes in their going out, and the wheels alongside them; and it stood [at the] entrance of [the] gate of [the] house of Yahweh the east, and [the] glory of [the] God of Israel [was] over them from above.
pieces: As I watched, the cherubim spread their wings and rose from the ground, and they went out with the wheels beside them. They halted at the entrance to the east gate of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house, with the glory of the God of Israel above them.

L.19: And the cherubim lifted up their wings and rose up from the earth before my eyes as they went out, with the wheels alongside them; and it stood at the entrance of the gate of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the eastern one; and the glory of the God of Israel [was] upon them from above.

R.19: As I watched, the cherubim spread their wings and rose from the ground. They left, and the wheels went with them. They stopped at the entrance of the east gate of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple. The glory of the God of Israel was above them.

decisions.choice: the east gate: the main gate of the temple, facing the Mount of Olives
decisions.reason: The temple's main entrance faced east. The glory pauses there before leaving the city (11:1, 22-23), and in the later vision it returns by the same gate (43:1-4), which is then shut (44:1-2).

decisions.choice: it stood: the whole throne, glory and creatures together, is the subject
decisions.reason: The verb is singular after the plural cherubim and wheels. The whole moving throne is treated as one.

decisions.choice: As I watched
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the common English expression for "before my eyes".

records.source: הִ֣יא הַחַיָּ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִ֛יתִי תַּ֥חַת אֱלֹהֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בִּֽנְהַר־כְּבָ֑ר וָאֵדַ֕ע כִּ֥י כְרוּבִ֖ים הֵֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: That [was] the living creature that I had seen beneath [the] God of Israel by [the] river Kebar; and I knew that cherubim they [were].
pieces: These were the living creatures I saw under the God of Israel at the Kebar Canal, and I knew that they were cherubim.

L.20: That [was] the living creature that I had seen beneath the God of Israel at the river Kebar; and I knew that cherubim they [were].

R.20: These were the same living creatures I had seen under the God of Israel beside the Kebar Canal. Now I knew that they were cherubim.

decisions.choice: "I knew that they were cherubim": the creatures of the Kebar vision are the cherubim of the temple (see 10:15)
decisions.reason: Ezekiel, a priest (1:3), knew the cherubim of the temple's carvings and of the ark. Now he understands that what he saw in Babylon was the LORD's own throne, borne by the cherubim, and that the LORD was present with the exiles.

decisions.choice: beneath the God of Israel: the creatures bear the throne of God
decisions.reason: The creatures were under the vault on which the throne stood (1:22-26). Ezekiel speaks here more directly than in chapter 1, where he described only "the likeness of the glory of the LORD" (1:28).

records.source: אַרְבָּעָ֨ה אַרְבָּעָ֤ה פָנִים֙ לְאֶחָ֔ד וְאַרְבַּ֥ע כְּנָפַ֖יִם לְאֶחָ֑ד וּדְמוּת֙ יְדֵ֣י אָדָ֔ם תַּ֖חַת כַּנְפֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Four, four faces to each one, and four wings to each one, and [the] likeness of hands of a human beneath their wings.
pieces: Each had four faces and four wings, and under their wings was something that looked like human hands.

L.21: Each one had four faces, and each one four wings, and the likeness of human hands [was] beneath their wings.

R.21: Each had four faces and four wings. Under their wings was something that looked like human hands.

decisions.choice: four faces, four wings, and hands like human hands: as in 1:6, 8
decisions.reason: The description repeats what Ezekiel saw in 1:6-8, again with the cautious "likeness" (see 1:28).

records.source: וּדְמ֣וּת פְּנֵיהֶ֔ם הֵ֣מָּה הַפָּנִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר רָאִ֨יתִי֙ עַל־נְהַר־כְּבָ֔ר מַרְאֵיהֶ֖ם וְאוֹתָ֑ם אִ֛ישׁ אֶל־עֵ֥בֶר פָּנָ֖יו יֵלֵֽכוּ׃
records.gloss: And [the] likeness of their faces, they [were] the faces that I had seen by [the] river Kebar, their appearance and they; each one straight ahead of his face they went.
pieces: As for their faces, they were the very faces I had seen by the Kebar Canal, in how they looked and in what they were. Each one went straight ahead.

L.22: And the likeness of their faces: they [were] the faces that I had seen by the river Kebar, their appearance and themselves; each one went straight ahead.

R.22: Their faces were the same faces I had seen by the Kebar Canal. Each of them moved straight ahead.

decisions.choice: their appearance and themselves: the faces were the same in look and in fact
alternatives: their appearance, and they went each straight ahead
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is very brief. It seems to say that the faces were not only like those of chapter 1 but the same ones. Some join "and they" to the clause that follows.

decisions.choice: each one went straight ahead: as 1:9, 12
decisions.reason: The same words describe the creatures in 1:9 and 1:12.
